result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. A new supplier with no terms gets 30, and terms can be changed on update. The full offline suite passes (176 suites, 0 failures), including a new test for the 45 → 14 renegotiation example. I haven't committed anything.

What changed:

- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier` gets `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30 CHECK (payment_terms_days >= 0)`.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new last component `paymentTermsDays`. The existing 5-argument constructor stays and defaults to 30, the same pattern `PurchaseOrder` uses. That keeps the ~80 existing call sites compiling without edits.
- **`DataStorePart01.java`**: create and update write the column. The by-name, by-country, by-minimum-rating listings read it.
- **`DataStorePart09.java`**: `findSupplierById` reads it, and so do the other supplier queries there (performance, spending, single-supplier categories).
- **`DataStorePart02.java`, `DataStorePart03.java`**: reorder suggestions and purchased-quantity-per-supplier also read it. Without this they would have silently shown 30 for every supplier.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: new test that registers a supplier at 45 days, renegotiates to 14, and checks the value in the name, country, rating and single-supplier lookups.

I did not add terms to the demo scenario output. The schema change applies at startup, so any file-based database created from the old schema would need the column added before it runs.
